reason: The cited evidence does not directly address surface-defect-driven melting onset in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles. E1 describes laser synthesis involving melting and fission but does not link surface defects to lowered melting barriers. E2 discusses defective edge planes as nucleation sites for nanoparticle formation, not as initiators of premelting in existing nanoparticles. Thus, the key premises lack specific prior support.
premises: Surface defects lower the local melting barrier in nanoparticles
Nanoparticles with higher surface defect densities begin partial melting at lower temperatures
Limited atomic mobility in small nanoparticles constrains complete melting
Defect-driven local melting leads to distinct morphological changes (splitting/coalescence)
Defect-free nanoparticles remain solid until near the bulk melting point
